title: Wire EDM 4-axis: per-ruling kerf widening, and a stated verify tolerance for tessellated twisted walls

body:
Part of #290. Found while building #537 (4-axis upper/lower profiles).

**What happens now.** A straight wire cannot touch a twisted (non-developable) ruled surface along its whole height. #537 keeps the kerf out by widening the kerf offset on both profile planes *uniformly* until the leaning kerf stands clear at every height read, and refuses past the op's `four_axis.tolerance`. Two costs follow:

1. The whole profile stands the widening proud of the kerf offset, though only the twisted stretches (e.g. the corners of a square-to-round) need it.
2. The wire laws (`sim::verify::wire`) judge the *mesh* with a 0.1 um tolerance. A model whose tessellation of a twisted wall bulges past the ruled surface between the two picked profiles (any STEP loft tessellated at a chord tolerance) is refused as a gouge - safe, but it blocks a correct cut of a real model.

**Wanted.**
- Widen per ruling (a variable offset along the profiles, with its own corner law) so the standing stock is only where the twist is; the path's note states the worst.
- A stated verify tolerance for a 4-axis cut (the op's own, visible on the report line) against which the wire laws judge the tessellated wall - never silent, never a default that hides a gouge.

Evidence: `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled.rs` (uniform widening), `docs/decisions/537-wire-4axis.md`; the #537 fixture meshes are split along the inner diagonal so they stand inside the ruled surface.

**Done means:** a square-to-round punch stands at the kerf offset on its straight stretches and widened only at the twist (pinned by a motion test reading both), and a lofted model tessellated at a stated chord tolerance posts when the op states a verify tolerance at least that large and is refused by name when it does not (pinned by an app test).
